question: At a licensed child care center in New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 3A:52), what is the staff/child ratio for children under 18 months of age while they are awake (not during rest or sleep)? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: The following staff/child ratios shall apply, except as specified in (d) through (f) below: Age Staff/Child Ratio Under 18 months 18 months up to 2 ½ years 2 ½ years up to 4 years 4 years 5 years and older 1:4 1:6 1:10 1:12 1:15
notes: During rest or sleep the ratio for under 18 months may be 1:10 when the 4.3(d) criteria are met. Centers where 50% or more of children have special needs: 1:3 under 2 1/2 years (4.3(e)). Infant groups are four infants per primary caregiver (4.4(a)2).

question: At a licensed child care center in New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 3A:52), what is the staff/child ratio for 3-year-olds (the rule's band of 2 1/2 years up to 4 years) while they are awake? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: The following staff/child ratios shall apply, except as specified in (d) through (f) below: Age Staff/Child Ratio Under 18 months 18 months up to 2 ½ years 2 ½ years up to 4 years 4 years 5 years and older 1:4 1:6 1:10 1:12 1:15
notes: The band runs from 2 1/2 up to 4 years. Maximum group 20 in early childhood programs (4.4(b)2). During rest or sleep, children 2 1/2 and above may be 1:20 when the 4.3(d) criteria are met.

question: At a licensed child care center in New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 3A:52), what is the staff/child ratio for 4-year-olds while they are awake? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: The following staff/child ratios shall apply, except as specified in (d) through (f) below: Age Staff/Child Ratio Under 18 months 18 months up to 2 ½ years 2 ½ years up to 4 years 4 years 5 years and older 1:4 1:6 1:10 1:12 1:15
notes: Maximum group 20 in early childhood programs. In mixed-age rooms, staff are computed per age group to the nearest tenth and any fraction over a whole number requires another staff member (4.3(h)).

question: At a licensed child care center in New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 3A:52), what is the staff/child ratio for children 5 years and older (including school-age children) while they are awake? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: The following staff/child ratios shall apply, except as specified in (d) through (f) below: Age Staff/Child Ratio Under 18 months 18 months up to 2 ½ years 2 ½ years up to 4 years 4 years 5 years and older 1:4 1:6 1:10 1:12 1:15
notes: 5 years and older is the oldest band. In school-age child care programs the maximum group is 30 (4.4(c)2) and only staff 16 or older count toward ratio (4.3(l)4).

question: In an early childhood program at a licensed child care center in New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 3A:52), what is the maximum group size for children 2 1/2 years of age and older (which includes 4-year-olds), outside the listed exceptions?
quote: For early childhood programs, the following shall apply for children 2 ½ years of age and older: ... Each group shall be limited to a maximum of 20 children except during meals, naptime, outdoor activities, specially-scheduled events
notes: Exceptions: meals, naptime, outdoor activities, specially-scheduled events, and daily information-sharing sessions such as circle time of no more than 15 minutes. School-age child care programs: maximum 30 (4.4(c)2).

question: In an early childhood program at a licensed child care center in New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 3A:52), what is the minimum age a staff member must be to be counted toward the staff/child ratio?
quote: The following minimum ages of staff members shall apply for purposes of computing the staff/child ratio: i. Only staff members who are at least 14 years of age shall be counted for the staff/child ratio;
notes: Staff under 16 may work only when school is not in session or as part of a school/work program; staff under 18 must be directly supervised by and visible to a staff member 18 or older (4.3(j)). School-age child care programs count only staff 16 or older (4.3(l)4).

question: For an early childhood program licensed to serve more than 30 children at a New Jersey child care center, what is the lowest degree that can qualify the director, and what experience must accompany it?
answer: A bachelor's degree plus one year of managerial or supervisory experience
quote: For early childhood programs licensed to serve more than 30 children, the director shall meet the qualification requirements specified in one of the options set forth in the chart below for education and experience: ... B Bachelor's Degree One year of managerial or supervisory experience
notes: Option A is a master's degree in a field related to children or business with no experience requirement. For programs licensed for 30 or fewer children the director needs group teacher qualifications; school-age programs need program supervisor qualifications.

question: How many hours of continuing staff development must each staff member at a New Jersey child care center complete each year (staff other than the director, head teachers, group teachers, and program supervisors)?
quote: The center shall ensure that all staff members who work at the center complete 12 hours of continuing staff development each year.
notes: The director, head teachers, group teachers and program supervisors need 20 hours a year instead (4.7(d)). Orientation training may count for six of the required hours (4.7(b)).

question: For a New Jersey child care center that began operating on or after July 1, 1989 and serves 16 or more children, what is the minimum usable activity indoor floor space per child?
quote: There shall be a minimum of 35 square feet of usable activity indoor floor space for each child in centers that began operating on or after July 1, 1989 and serve 16 or more children.
notes: 30 square feet per child for centers that began operating before July 1, 1989, or later centers serving fewer than 16 children (5.3(q)3i). Hallways, toilets, offices, storage, kitchens and similar areas are excluded.

question: For a new or relocating New Jersey child care center licensed on or after September 1, 2013 (children over 10 months attending three or more consecutive hours), how many additional square feet of net outdoor space are required for each child beyond 10 using the space at one time?
unit: square feet per additional child using the space at one time
quote: New and relocating centers licensed on or after September 1, 2013, shall provide a minimum of 350 square feet of net outdoor space. When more than 10 children are using such a space at one time, there shall be an additional 35 square feet of net outdoor space for each additional child
notes: Counted per child using the space at one time, on top of a 350 sq ft minimum. Existing centers: 150 sq ft minimum plus 30 sq ft for each child beyond five. The requirement can be waived when compliance is impossible and an indoor active play area is provided (5.4(a)7iv).

question: What is the maximum hot tap water temperature in an early childhood program at a New Jersey child care center?
quote: A supply of hot tap water not exceeding 110 degrees Fahrenheit and cold running water shall be provided.
notes: School-age child care programs: hot tap water not exceeding 120°F (5.5(a)3).

question: What must a New Jersey child care center receive before it administers medication or a health care procedure to a child?
answer: Written approval from the child's parent
quote: Medication and health care procedures shall be administered only after receipt of written approval from the child's parent(s).
notes: For long-term medication for a chronic condition the center also needs a written statement from a health care provider (7.5(b)8).

question: How often must a New Jersey licensed child care center conduct fire drills?
quote: The center shall conduct fire drills at least once a month, as specified in the NJUFC.
notes: Drills must be held during each session the center offers, one per year during nap time if applicable, and all children must be out of the building within three minutes (5.3(n)2).

question: How long must a New Jersey child care center keep a child's records after the child is no longer enrolled?
unit: year after the child is no longer enrolled
quote: Children's records shall be maintained on file for one year after the child is no longer enrolled at the center.
notes: Staff records: one year after the staff member stops working at the center; all other records: one year after made or received unless otherwise specified.

question: In what position must a New Jersey child care center initially place children 12 months of age and younger for sleep?
answer: Face-up (on the back), unless the child's health care provider indicates a different position in writing
quote: For children 12 months of age and younger, the center shall ensure that each child is initially placed in a face-up sleeping position unless a different position is indicated in writing by the child's health care provider.
notes: 'Face-up' means on the back. Swaddling during rest and sleep is prohibited (6.4(a)3).

question: By when must a New Jersey child care center report to the Office of Licensing an injury to a child under its supervision that results in the child's admission to a hospital?
answer: By the next working day after the center learns of it (with documentation within one week)
quote: shall report the following occurrences to the Office of Licensing by the next working day after the center learns of the occurrence ... 2. The occurrence of an injury or illness while under the center's supervision that results in a child's admittance to the hospital;
notes: Deadline is to the licensing agency; written documentation is due within one week. The same rule covers ER visits, deaths, and 911/urgent care calls. Parents must be told immediately of bites that break the skin, head injuries, falls from a height, or injuries needing medical care (7.6(a)).

question: For a child in an early childhood program who is not enrolled in a public or private school, when must a New Jersey child care center have the child's immunization record on file?
quote: For each child not enrolled in a public or private school, upon admission, the center shall maintain on file at the center a Universal Child Health Record (Department of Health Form CH-14) or its equivalent, updated annually, along with an immunization record
notes: A 30-day grace period applies to children coming from other states or countries and to children in foster care or experiencing homelessness.

question: How many staff members with current first aid and CPR certification must be in a New Jersey child care center at all times when enrolled children are present?
quote: At least two staff members who have current certified basic knowledge of first aid principles and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), as defined by a recognized health organization (such as the American Red Cross), shall be in the center at all times when enrolled children are present.
notes: First aid and CPR training must include a hands-on component (5.3(o)2).

question: How long is each licensing period for a New Jersey licensed child care center?
quote: Each licensing period, which may include the issuance of one or more temporary licenses and/or one regular license, shall be three years.
notes: Temporary licenses last at most six months each and a center may not operate on temporary licenses for more than 18 months (2.2(c)). Renewal applications are due at least 45 days before expiration (2.1(b)).

question: During rest or sleep at a licensed child care center in New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 3A:52), when the rule's naptime staffing criteria are met, what staff/child ratio applies to children 2 1/2 years and above? Answer as children per staff member.
quote: The following staff/child ratios shall apply during rest or sleep, when the criteria listed in (d) 1, 2, and 3 below are met: Age Staff/Child Ratio Under 18 months 18 months to under 2 ½ years 2 ½ years and above 1:10 1:12 1:20
notes: Criteria: a staff member physically present in the nap area who can summon others without leaving; enough staff in the facility to meet awake ratios; naptime preparations complete with all children 18 months+ resting or sleeping and all under 18 months sleeping.

question: What is the minimum number of staff members who must accompany children on any field trip from a New Jersey child care center, even when the ratios would allow fewer?
quote: There shall be a minimum of two staff members accompanying children on any field trip, outing, or special event involving children away from the center, even when the appropriate staff/child ratios allow fewer than two staff members.

question: How many hours of staff development must the director, head teachers, group teachers, and program supervisors at a New Jersey child care center each complete per year?
quote: In lieu of the child care staff development specified in (b) above, the director, head teacher(s), group teacher(s), and program supervisor(s) shall each complete 20 hours of staff development each year.
notes: Other staff need 12 hours (4.7(c)). Directors must also complete licensing-regulation training within 90 days of hire, which can count toward the 20 hours (4.7(e)).

question: In a school-age child care program at a New Jersey licensed child care center, what is the minimum age a staff member must be to be counted toward the staff/child ratio?
quote: For school-age child care programs, the following shall apply: ... Only staff members who are at least 16 years of age shall be counted for the staff/child ratio.
notes: Early childhood programs count staff from age 14 (4.3(k)2i). With six or more children present, a school-age program needs at least two staff members, one of them 18 or older (4.3(l)1).

question: Within how many minutes must all children present be evacuated from the building during each fire drill at a New Jersey child care center?
quote: The center shall ensure that all children present are evacuated from the building within three minutes during each fire drill.
